streamOpenAIResponses/streamSimpleOpenAIResponses/compactOpenAIResponses/try_compact_openai_responses/createClient/buildParams/getCompat/getPromptCacheRetention/resolveCacheRetention/applyServiceTierPricing/getServiceTierCostMultiplier + local SSE buffer. The OpenAI SDK is replaced by reqwest: base URL + /responses, same headers (session_id, x-client-request-id, copilot, cloudflare cf-aig-authorization, opencode), same JSON body keys/defaults.

Whole file: -stats + cache API/resolveCodexUrl/resolveCodexWebSocketUrl/parseErrorResponse/extractAccountId/createCodexRequestId/buildBaseCodexHeaders/buildSSEHeaders/buildWebSocketHeaders/codexUsageLimitMessage/resolveCodexServiceTier/applyServiceTierPricing/normalizeCodexStatus. reqwest only. One gap: no WebSocket crate exists in the workspace, so the socket comes from set_web_socket_constructor (None by default). With no constructor connectWebSocket fails with the exact TS message 'WebSocket transport is not available in this runtime', which drives the real fallback path (diagnostic + recordWebSocketFailure + recordWebSocketSseFallback) and then SSE. mapCodexEvents throws via an Arc<Mutex<Option<CodexThrown>>> slot because a Rust stream cannot reject; the caller re-raises it at the same point in the catch boundary.

Post-build fixes I applied to my files: (1) BoxFuture has no lifetime parameter -> BoxFuture<Result<Value, CompactionRequestError>>; (2) parse_sse_response / map_codex_events / parse_web_socket / start_web_socket_output_on_first_event now return Pin<Box<dyn Stream<..> + Send>> so the Unfold combinator is Unpin and the Item types line up with ResponsesEventStream; (3) process_web_socket_stream takes on_start: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> (was an impl-Fn parameter that could not outlive the async body); (4) openai_responses_shared.rs: parse_streaming_json returns Value, so ToolCall::new now receives match args { Value::Object(map) => map, _ => Map::new() }.
honest_summary: openai_responses_shared.rs, openai_responses.rs and openai_codex_responses.rs are complete 1:1 ports with unit tests (parsing, serialisation, ordering, error mapping, thresholds, header building, defaults, cached-context delta, fallback diagnostics) and no real network calls. azure_openai_responses.rs is the lead's file, not mine. The one real functional gap is the WebSocket transport in the Codex provider: no WebSocket crate exists in the workspace, so the socket is injectable and defaults to 'unavailable', reproducing the TypeScript's no-WebSocket runtime path exactly (same error message, same reconnect/fallback bookkeeping) and landing on SSE.
